input.summary: The owner asks whether netem packet delivery rate can substitute for optical-terminal availability over LEO passes. It cannot: built-in runners measure packet transport only and implement no orbital, atmospheric, or optical-propagation model. Three key decisions are needed before a feasible pilot can be designed.
clarification_questions: How is '99.99% availability over LEO passes' operationally defined — e.g., fraction of pass-seconds with a usable optical link, fraction of passes with at least one successful acquisition, or another metric — and what evidence type is intended to measure it (physical terminal observations, a named atmospheric/orbital simulation model with a versioned input dataset, or something else)?

Do you have access to any applicable versioned model or archived dataset (e.g., a cloud-cover climatology, link-margin simulation, or terminal acquisition log) that could serve as the input to a pilot? If so, please supply its identity, version, and a SHA-256 digest so it can be referenced in the protocol.

If no optical model or terminal observations are available now, is the intended path (a) wait until hardware/observations are available for a new-empirical measurement pilot, (b) identify and supply a simulation model/input for a model-output pilot, or (c) something else? This decision determines which experiment type and data_origin are applicable.
